comments.author: Misun
comments.body: So can somebody explain to me how these + and - indications work in combination with in-game backstock information. Example. Plague in Macau, foodstuffs at -6, but let's say in-game backstock is currently high. To trade or not to trade?

comments.author: ReaD
comments.body:
when certain condition happen in 1 town like plague in macau...things like Foodstuffs / Livestock / Luxury Goods will have their backstock go down...

and trading something that is needed(Foodstuffs / Livestock / Luxury Goods ) while in certain condition like plague give bonus or 2 times more value on cultural points...

but you kinda need to wait for a little bit till the backstock chart in nanban merchant really low and then do the nanban....

sometimes..with the help of nanban purveyor certificate...you may get 1:1.2 rate(i do and i don't have that ship skill yet)..but not all the times since i still kinda need to figure out how to get it all the times..

tl:dr
condition happen(plague) -> bring something that give bonus(Foodstuffs / Livestock / Luxury Goods ) -> wait for backstock getting really low -> get 2x cultural point -> ??? -> profit...

comments.author: Liza
comments.body: the plusses and minuses are modifiers that influence the backstock. It's a lot like the arrows at the merchant, if market is crashed and prices are currently at 50%, you don't really care if the price is trending up or down, you don't sell. You trade according to what the backstock is, not what it's going to be later on.

comments.author: Claudia
comments.body: The percents indicates the starting backstock when port was opened, after that its modified by events and player interventions. Is a roughly stimation of the average backstock if no one trades, in a port most goods type has lowering ammounts of goods (so a starting baseline of 30% can eventually drop to almost 0, and even when a lot of players sells that type of goods to barter, backstock will never be very high). Also, there are few goods that the town exports and almost always growing, naturally can reach almost max backstock and by player buying can eventually drop to the baseline, but hardly will be a lot lower.
